formation.title: Restoration of the Mongol Empire
formation.text:
The dream of Genghis Khan lives again. From the ruins of fragmented khanates, a single ruler has united the steppe peoples and claimed dominion over the lands between the four seas. The kurultai has spoken, and the world's largest empire is reborn.

But the question remains: what kind of empire shall this be? Will we follow the path of eternal war, riding as our ancestors did beneath the Eternal Blue Sky, bringing all nations under the hooves of our cavalry? Or shall we build an empire of law and commerce, where the Silk Road flourishes under Mongol peace, and every culture finds a place in the Khan's court?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We ride beneath the Eternal Blue Sky!

modifiers.name: Way of the Eternal Blue Sky
modifiers.text: Under the banner of the Eternal Blue Sky, the Mongol hordes ride as one. Every horizon is a frontier, every steppe a highway for the horsemen of the Khan. The world trembles before warriors who sleep in the saddle and loose arrows at the gallop.

options.text: We shall wear the Crown of the World.

modifiers.name: Crown of the World
modifiers.text: The Mongol Empire is more than conquest: it is a bridge between civilizations. From the Pacific to the Mediterranean, merchants travel under the protection of the Khan, scholars exchange knowledge across continents, and a hundred tongues speak in the markets of Karakorum.

advances.name: Steppe Horsemanship
advances.text: The Mongol warrior is born in the saddle. Children learn to ride before they can walk, and every herder is a potential cavalryman.

advances.name: Composite Bow Craft
advances.text: The Mongol composite bow (fashioned from horn, sinew, and wood) can deliver lethal force at distances exceeding 400 meters, giving mounted archers a decisive advantage.

advances.name: The Great Yasa
advances.text: Genghis Khan's supreme law code binds all subjects equally, establishing universal order across the vast territories of the empire.

event.title: The Great Yasa
event.text:
The Khan has decreed that the Great Yasa, the supreme law code first proclaimed by Genghis Khan himself, shall be enforced across all territories of the empire. This code, which prescribes absolute loyalty to the Khan, severe punishment for theft and adultery, religious tolerance, and the inviolability of ambassadors, forms the legal backbone of Mongol rule.

Under the Yasa, there is no distinction between the law that governs a Mongol noble and that which governs a Persian merchant or a Chinese scholar. All subjects are equal before the Khan's justice. This radical universalism has earned both admiration and fear: for the penalties are harsh, but the order they bring is undeniable.

options.text: Let the Yasa bring order to all lands.

modifiers.name: The Great Yasa Proclaimed
modifiers.text: The Khan has proclaimed the Great Yasa across all lands, establishing a universal code that binds noble and commoner, Mongol and foreigner alike.

options.text: The Yasa shall be enforced by the sword.

modifiers.name: Yasa Enforcement
modifiers.text: The Great Yasa is enforced with iron discipline across all territories of the empire. Where the law is obeyed, order prevails. And those who defy it meet swift justice.

advances.name: Noyan Command
advances.text: The Noyan, commanders of thousands, form the officer corps of the Mongol military, directing tumens with discipline that transcends tribal loyalties.

advances.name: Felt Ger Encampments
advances.text: Mobile felt tents, the ger, allow Mongol armies to establish and relocate camps with remarkable speed, ensuring troops remain supplied even deep in enemy territory.

advances.name: Wolf Hunt Tactics
advances.text: The nerge, the great hunt, trains Mongol warriors in the art of encirclement and coordinated pursuit, tactics that translate directly to the battlefield.

advances.name: Ortaq Partnerships
advances.text: Mongol princes invest capital in merchant partnerships with Muslim and Uighur traders, creating a commercial network that spans the empire.

advances.name: Tumen Discipline
advances.text: The tumen, a unit of ten thousand, operates with coordinated precision, each subdivision responding instantly to signal flags and drumbeats across the battlefield.

advances.name: Mongol Siege Corps
advances.text: Mongol commanders recruit Chinese and Muslim engineers to build trebuchets, battering rams, and other siege engines, turning a cavalry army into a force that can reduce any fortification.

advances.name: Darughachi Governors
advances.text: The darughachi, Mongol-appointed governors, administer conquered territories, conducting censuses, collecting taxes, and maintaining the Khan's authority across diverse populations.

advances.name: Silk Road Protection
advances.text: Mongol cavalry patrols ensure the safety of Silk Road caravans, and toll stations collect revenue while guaranteeing merchants safe passage through the empire's vast territories.

advances.name: Kurultai Assembly
advances.text: The Kurultai, the great assembly of Mongol chiefs and generals, deliberates on matters of succession, war, and law, providing legitimacy to the Khan's rule.

advances.name: Pax Mongolica Trade
advances.text: Under Mongol peace, the Silk Road reaches its apex. Goods, technologies, and ideas flow freely between East and West across the largest contiguous land empire in history.

event.title: The Peace of the Mongols
event.text:
For the first time in history, a single power controls the entire length of the Silk Road. Caravans laden with silk, spices, porcelain, and precious metals travel from the China Sea to the shores of the Mediterranean without changing hands or paying rival tolls. Genoese merchants deal directly with Chinese traders, Persian astronomers correspond with Mongol princes, and technologies flow in every direction.

The ortaq merchant partnerships, financed by Mongol princes and staffed by Muslim and Uighur traders, have created a commercial network of unprecedented scale. Paper money circulates alongside silver, and the Yam postal system carries not only official dispatches but mercantile correspondence across the vast reaches of the empire.

options.text: The roads of the Khan bring prosperity to all.

modifiers.name: Pax Mongolica Flourishing
modifiers.text: Under the peace enforced by Mongol cavalry, the greatest trade network in history stretches from Beijing to Baghdad. Merchants travel in safety, and goods flow freely along the Silk Road.

options.text: Let the caravans pay tribute for safe passage.

modifiers.name: Silk Road Taxation
modifiers.text: Mongol toll stations along the Silk Road extract tribute from every caravan that travels under the Khan's protection, turning the peace of the empire into a steady stream of revenue.

advances.name: Religious Tolerance
advances.text: The Mongol Empire grants freedom of worship to all subjects. Buddhist, Muslim, Christian, and Tengrist communities coexist under the Khan's protection.

advances.name: Counterweight Trebuchet
advances.text: Persian engineers Ismail and Al-aud-Din construct counterweight trebuchets capable of hurling 300-kilogram projectiles over 500 meters, revolutionizing Mongol siege warfare.

advances.name: Paper Currency
advances.text: The Mongol Empire issues paper banknotes backed by imperial authority, facilitating commerce across territories where silver and gold are scarce.

advances.name: Horse Relay Posts
advances.text: The Ortoo relay stations, spaced every thirty miles across the empire, allow messages to traverse the entire length of the Silk Road in a matter of days.

advances.name: Keshig Guard
advances.text: The Keshig, ten thousand elite warriors chosen from the sons of generals and chiefs, serve as the Khan's personal guard, household, and most trusted military force.

event.title: The Keshig: Sword of the Khan
event.text:
The Keshig, the Khan's imperial guard, represents the finest warriors of the Mongol Empire. Originally numbering just seventy day-guards and eighty night-guards under Genghis Khan, the Keshig has grown into a force of ten thousand elite soldiers, each handpicked from the sons of generals and tribal chiefs.

A member of the Keshig outranks every other military officer in the empire, save only the Khan himself. They serve as the Khan's personal bodyguard, his household servants, his administrative core, and his shock troops in battle. To serve in the Keshig is the highest honor a warrior can achieve. And to fail in that service means death.

options.text: The Keshig guard shall never falter.

advances.name: Mangudai Tactics
advances.text: The mangudai, specialized light cavalry skirmishers, feign retreat to lure enemies into ambush, then wheel and deliver devastating arrow barrages at close range.

advances.name: Silk Road Caravanserai
advances.text: Grand roadside inns offer shelter, food, and stabling for merchants traveling the Silk Road, supporting the vast commercial network of the empire.

advances.name: Imperial Armory
advances.text:
Centralized weapon workshops mass-produce standardized arms and armor for the Mongol military, ensuring every warrior is equipped to the Khan's specifications.

Available in: Composite Bow Workshop

advances.name: Gunpowder Adaptation
advances.text: Mongol engineers adapt Chinese gunpowder weapons for steppe warfare, developing lighter firearms suited to the mobility of horse-mounted infantry.

event.title: Thunder on the Steppe
event.text:
The Mongol Empire has always excelled at absorbing the military technologies of conquered peoples. Chinese engineers built our first siege weapons; Muslim artisans perfected our trebuchets. Now the empire turns its attention to the newest revolution in warfare: gunpowder firearms.

Mongol smiths and captured engineers have developed handheld firearms suited to steppe warfare: lighter than European muskets, carried by mounted infantry who can dismount to deliver devastating volleys before remounting and withdrawing. The thunder of the Khan's guns echoes across the plains, heralding a new age of Mongol military power.

options.text: Let the thunder of our guns shake the earth!

modifiers.name: Thunder of the Khan
modifiers.text: Mongol engineers have mastered gunpowder weapons, adapting Chinese and Muslim technologies into a devastating arsenal that combines the mobility of the steppe with the destructive power of cannon fire.

options.text: Share this knowledge for the prosperity of the realm.

modifiers.name: Gunpowder Prosperity
modifiers.text: The knowledge of gunpowder weapons is shared across the empire, spurring innovation in production, construction, and trade as the new technology transforms civilian life alongside the military.

advances.name: Universal Chronicle
advances.text: Imperial historians compile comprehensive chronicles of every conquered people, preserving knowledge from China to Persia in the tradition of Rashid al-Din's Compendium of Chronicles.

advances.name: Eternal Empire
advances.text: The Mongol Empire preserves and transmits the cultural achievements of all its subject peoples, creating a legacy that transcends any single civilization.

advances.name: Steppe Modernization
advances.text: The empire adapts modern production techniques to the vast scale of its territories, combining industrial capacity with the logistical traditions of the steppe.

advances.name: Legacy of Conquest
advances.text: The martial traditions of Genghis Khan endure into the modern age. Mongol cavalry, though changed by centuries of evolution, remains a formidable force on any battlefield.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Mongol Empire
destiny.text: The Mongol Empire has risen again. Maintain stability as the Khan charts the empire's course through history.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Empire Restored
event.text: The Mongol Empire stands reborn, a colossus spanning the breadth of Asia. The kurultai has affirmed the Khan's authority, and the people look to their ruler to guide this vast dominion toward its destiny. Whether through the thunder of hooves or the quiet hum of commerce, the empire's path forward will be written in the annals of history.

options.text: The world awaits the Khan's will.

destiny.name: The Western Ride
destiny.text: Complete the work of Hulagu Khan. Bring Baghdad and Damascus under Mongol dominion, extending the empire's reach into the heart of the Islamic world.

conditions.text: Chose Way of the Eternal Blue Sky
Own Baghdad, or a subject owns it
Own Damascus, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Western Ride Begins
event.text: Mongol banners fly over Baghdad and Damascus, cities that once defied the horde and now bow before the Khan. The Abbasid caliphate's former seat of power is Mongol ground, and the ancient crossroads of the Levant carry the thunder of steppe cavalry. The western frontier of the empire has been pushed beyond what even Hulagu achieved.

options.text: From the Tigris to the Euphrates, all is ours.

destiny.name: The Southern Campaign
destiny.text: Turn the conquering gaze southward. The riches of India have long tempted Mongol khans: seize Delhi and Lahore to bring the subcontinent into the empire.

conditions.text: Own Delhi, or a subject owns it
Own Lahore, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Gates of India
event.text:
Delhi has fallen. The subcontinent's riches (its elephants, its spices, its teeming millions) now flow into the Mongol sphere. What the Chagatai khans attempted and failed, the restored empire has achieved. The Khyber Pass echoes with the hooves of the Khan's cavalry, and the sultans of Hindustan kneel before a power greater than any they have known.

How shall the Khan consolidate these southern conquests?

options.text: Establish swift cavalry supply lines.

modifiers.name: Swift Cavalry Doctrine
modifiers.text: The Khan's cavalry supply lines stretch from the Indus to the Ganges, with relay stations ensuring rapid reinforcement and resupply across the conquered territories.

options.text: Let our name strike terror in their hearts.

modifiers.name: Terror of the Steppe
modifiers.text: The mere approach of Mongol banners causes cities to surrender without a fight. The Khan's reputation precedes his armies, though the constant warfare leaves little time for scholarly pursuits.

destiny.name: Empire of the Four Seas
destiny.text: The ultimate vision of Genghis Khan: an empire stretching from sea to sea. Take Constantinople, Cairo, and Buda to prove Mongol supremacy across three continents.

conditions.text: Own Constantinople, or a subject owns it
Own Cairo, or a subject owns it
Own Buda, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75

event.title: Lord of the Four Seas
event.text:
Constantinople, Cairo, Buda (three cities that represent three continents, three civilizations, three millennia of history) all fly the banner of the Khan. The Mongol Empire now stretches from the Pacific to the Mediterranean, from the Arctic tundra to the Nile Delta. No empire in history has matched this scale.

The Khan stands at the pinnacle of earthly power. How shall this supreme achievement be commemorated?

options.text: The conquest shall never end.

modifiers.name: World Conqueror
modifiers.text: The Khan commands the greatest military machine in history. Armies are maintained at reduced cost, and noble levies swell with warriors eager to serve the conqueror of the known world.

options.text: Bring peace through the sword's authority.

modifiers.name: Pax by the Sword
modifiers.text: The Khan imposes order on conquered lands through firm but fair governance. Conquered peoples are integrated into the empire, and the estates find satisfaction under Mongol rule.

destiny.name: The Silk Road Renewed
destiny.text: Under Mongol peace, the Silk Road flourishes once more. Ensure silk flows through the capital market and fill the imperial treasury with the tolls of the caravans.

conditions.text: Chose Crown of the World
The capital

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

conditions.text: Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Silk Road Lives Again
event.text: Silk caravans wind through the empire's heartland once more, protected by Mongol cavalry and taxed by Mongol governors. The capital's markets overflow with fine cloth from China, gemstones from Persia, and spices from every corner of the known world. The imperial treasury grows fat with the tolls of a thousand caravan routes.

options.text: The merchants prosper under the Khan's peace.

destiny.name: Exchange of Civilizations
destiny.text: The empire bridges East and West, facilitating the greatest exchange of knowledge in history. Tabriz, where the scholars of Persia, China and the Franks once worked on one history of the world, is built up again, and a library is raised there, as in Rashid al-Din's quarter, so that what the scholars write is copied and spread.

conditions.text: Tabriz is ours and has been built up to a development of at least 29
Tabriz is ours and has a Library
Prestige at least 50

event.title: The Great Exchange
event.text:
Under Mongol rule, an unprecedented exchange of knowledge spans the continent. Chinese astronomers correspond with Persian mathematicians, Uighur scribes translate Greek philosophy, and the copyists of Tabriz send learning out in a dozen languages. The empire has become not merely a political entity but a conduit for civilization itself.

How shall the Khan direct this flowering of knowledge?

options.text: Found schools to spread learning across the realm.

modifiers.name: Schools of the East
modifiers.text: The empire's schools and observatories drive institutional progress and social advancement, though the scholarly focus draws attention away from military tradition.

options.text: Empower merchants as patrons of knowledge.

modifiers.name: Merchant Princes
modifiers.text: Empowered merchant houses dominate the empire's trade centers, driving prosperity and commercial activity across the vast Silk Road network.

destiny.name: Universal Dominion
destiny.text: The Mongol Empire aspires to become the seat of universal civilization. Karakorum, the capital of Ogedei, is rebuilt as a city, the treasury is filled, and gems adorn the capital market.

conditions.text: Karakorum is ours and has grown into a city
Gold at least 3000
Prestige at least 75
The capital

children.text: Gems is produced in the market
Gems is traded in the market

event.title: The Crown of All Nations
event.text:
The Mongol Empire has achieved what no other power in history has accomplished: a true universal state where every culture contributes, every tradition is preserved, and every people finds their place under the protection of the Khan. Karakorum stands again as a city to rival the greatest of any age, and the treasury overflows with the wealth of a continent.

What legacy shall the Khan leave to the ages?

options.text: Build the eternal road of prosperity.

modifiers.name: The Eternal Road
modifiers.text: The Silk Road has become more than a trade route: it is the artery of civilization itself. Raw materials flow freely, populations grow, and religious harmony prevails across the empire.

options.text: Become the Khan of all peoples.

modifiers.name: Khan of All Peoples
modifiers.text: The Khan rules as sovereign of every nation within the empire, expanding diplomatic reach and fostering universal literacy, though the openness of the realm complicates intelligence operations.

units.name: Steppe Horse Archer
units.text: Mounted archers raised from the Mongol steppe, trained from childhood in the saddle. Every man of the household rides, each with his string of remounts, and they rain arrows on enemies while remaining frustratingly out of reach.

units.name: Wolf Raider
units.text: Light cavalry trained in the nerge, the great hunt, specializing in encirclement and pursuit. They strike with the coordinated ferocity of a wolf pack.

units.name: Tumen Heavy Cavalry
units.text: The armored heart of a Mongol tumen: heavy cavalry equipped with lances, sabers, and lamellar armor, capable of delivering devastating shock charges.

units.name: Mongol Siege Engineer
units.text: Chinese and Muslim engineers recruited into Mongol service, operating trebuchets and other siege engines that reduce even the mightiest fortifications to rubble.

units.name: Counterweight Trebuchet
units.text: A hinged counterweight trebuchet designed by Persian engineers, capable of hurling massive projectiles with devastating accuracy over great distances.

units.name: Keshig Guard
units.text: The Khan's elite imperial guard: ten thousand warriors of proven loyalty, trained in every form of combat, who serve as both personal bodyguard and shock troops.

units.name: Mangudai Skirmisher
units.text: Light cavalry masters of the feigned retreat. They lure enemies into pursuit, then wheel to deliver punishing arrow volleys before melting away across the steppe.

units.name: Mongol Handgunner
units.text: Mongol infantry armed with adapted gunpowder weapons, combining the devastating firepower of firearms with the mobile tactics of steppe warfare.

units.name: Legacy Steppe Cavalry
units.text: The direct descendants of Genghis Khan's horsemen, carrying forward centuries of cavalry tradition into the modern age with characteristic Mongol mobility.

buildings.name: Composite Bow Workshop
buildings.text: A specialized workshop where master bowyers craft the legendary Mongol composite bow from layers of horn, sinew, and birch wood.

buildings.name: Ger Encampment
buildings.text: A permanent base of felt ger tents that serves as a staging point and supply depot for Mongol armies operating deep in the field.

buildings.name: Ortaq Trading House
buildings.text: A partnership office where Mongol princes and Muslim merchants coordinate the vast commercial enterprises that span the empire's trade routes.

buildings.name: Kurultai Hall
buildings.text: A grand assembly hall where Mongol chiefs, generals, and nobles gather to deliberate on matters of war, succession, and the governance of the empire.

buildings.name: Imperial Mint
buildings.text: A facility for printing paper currency backed by the full authority of the Khan, facilitating commerce across the empire's vast territories.

buildings.name: Ortoo Relay Station
buildings.text: A horse relay station in the Yam postal network, where messengers exchange mounts to carry dispatches across the empire at remarkable speed.

buildings.name: Caravanserai
buildings.text: A large roadside inn offering food, lodging, and stabling to Silk Road merchants, serving as a hub for trade and information along the empire's highways.

buildings.name: Khan's Archive
buildings.text: A repository of knowledge gathered from every corner of the empire: Chinese scrolls, Persian manuscripts, and Mongol oral histories preserved for future generations.

buildings.name: Mongol War Camp
buildings.text: A permanent military staging point in the tradition of Genghis Khan's great encampments, equipped to raise, supply, and launch armies across the empire's vast frontiers.

buildings.name: House of Wisdom
buildings.text: A grand center of learning inspired by the legendary Bayt al-Hikma of Baghdad, rebuilt under Mongol patronage as a repository for the knowledge of every civilization under the Khan's rule.

list.name: The Great Yasa
list.text: The Yeke Jasaq is the customary law promulgated by Chinggis Khan and elaborated under Ogedei. It binds the imperial clan, the army, and the subject peoples alike, fixing the death penalty for theft and adultery, regulating the hunt, and ordering the keshig. Its scrolls are read aloud at every kuriltai. While the law is upheld, steppe discipline holds; once neglected, contradictory rulings and dynastic appeals erode the compact between the khan and his tribes.

neglected.name: Horde Unity Change on Ruler Death

list.name: Kuriltai Assembly
list.text: The kuriltai is the great assembly of the imperial clan and senior noyans, summoned to elect a new khan, ratify campaigns, and divide spoils. From Onon in 1206 to Karakorum in 1251, no Mongol throne is uncontested without it. The assembly legitimises the khan but also fragments imperial decision-making: the partition of the empire after Mongke's death in 1259 is the kuriltai's greatest failure.

neglected.name: Horde Unity Change on Ruler Death

list.name: Keshig Imperial Guard
list.text: The keshig is Chinggis's ten-thousand-strong household corps, divided into the turqaut day guard and the kebte'ul night guard. It is at once the khan's bodyguard, his personal staff, and the training school for future commanders and darughachi. Recruitment takes the sons of noyans as hostages, transmuting hereditary aristocracy into chosen royal servants. When neglected, the corps becomes a gilded clique and hereditary capture closes the inner court.

list.name: Yam Postal Network
list.text: The yam is a system of relay stations spaced roughly a day's hard ride apart, manned by ortoochi keepers who supply fresh mounts to imperial messengers bearing paiza tablets of authority. Marco Polo describes it as the wonder of the empire: news, decrees, tax registers, and merchants move across continental distances in weeks rather than months. The network is funded by the qubchur tax and corvee labour levied from peasant communities along the routes, a burden they bitterly resent but cannot refuse.

list.name: Darughachi Governance
list.text: A darughachi (basqaq in Turkic usage) is a Mongol-appointed resident commissioner placed over a conquered city or vassal court. He takes the census, levies the tamgha customs, conscripts artisans for imperial workshops, and forwards the tribute owed to the Great Khan. Unlike timar or jagir holders, the darughachi holds no land and may be transferred at will: the office is deliberately detached from local elites to prevent its capture, and Russian and Persian chronicles record it as the heaviest of imperial burdens.

list.name: Yelu Chucai's Synthesis
list.text: Yelu Chucai, a Khitan scholar inherited from the Jin chancery, convinced Ogedei Khan that taxing the settled population was more lucrative than slaughtering it. Under his stewardship the court adopts Liao-Jin fiscal practice: registered households, fixed silver and silk levies, scribal record-keeping in Chinese, and Confucian-trained clerks in place of tribal accountants. The reform requires the command of a sedentary capital (Karakorum or Dadu) and alienates the steppe nobility, who lose their right to plunder freely.
